Under POL-COLL-004 §4.2, reduced hours or pay counts as financial hardship. Before asking for any payment, the agent must acknowledge the hardship, record hardship_flag with the stated reason, and offer at least one eligible hardship option. Examples include the 3-month reduced payment (HP-LOAN-RED3: pay 50% of the regular payment for 3 months), a reduced card minimum payment, a reduced interest rate or skipping a payment. The agent must also not ask for a payment the customer has said they can't afford. QA checks this as a critical item (item 7), and the mid-stage script says the same at step 4. Customers in bankruptcy or a consumer proposal are not eligible for these options.

answer: Our current policies say nothing about suing a customer or referring them for legal action, at two missed payments or at any other point, so they neither allow nor forbid it. That decision needs to go to Legal or Collections policy owners. What the policies do say: agents must not threaten legal action, garnishment or arrest on calls (qa_checklist item 4). If the customer reports hardship, the agent must offer at least one eligible hardship option before asking for payment (POL-COLL-004 §4.2). If the customer has filed for bankruptcy or a consumer proposal, a stay of proceedings stops all collection activity (POL-COLL-001 §7.3). If the amount is disputed, payment requests for that amount pause until the dispute is resolved (PRC-COLL-012 §6.1).

answer: The 3-month reduced payment programme (HP-LOAN-RED3) lasts 3 months. During that time the customer pays 50% of their regular payment, so the payment is cut by half. Interest keeps building up, and the unpaid amount is added to the end of the loan term. It covers personal loans, auto loans and lines of credit, and the account can be at most 90 days past due. The agent FAQ says the programme lasts 6 months, but that conflicts with the policy, and the policy takes priority. The old v4.1 policy (40% off for 2 months) has been replaced and no longer applies.
